summary: Klamath NF ground cabin in the Marble Mountain Wilderness, built 1934 per the register (a 1935 CCC date is also given), dismantled 1979; nothing remains at the site.

facts.design: Ground cabin to California Region 5 Plan BC-301; a 1952 survey describes a standard Forest Service single-story lookout house about 14 feet square
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1979; the register says nothing remains at the site
facts.agency: Klamath National Forest, US Forest Service

access.note: Inside the Marble Mountain Wilderness; the Six Rivers National Forest page says no wilderness permit is needed to enter

events.note: Site selected as a lookout site, replacing Marble Mountain
Ground cabin built to Plan BC-301; a June 1934 paper says work was to start the next week; a Klamath chronology quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 1935 for CCC construction
Staffed full time 1955-60; otherwise staffed as needed
Blue Lake Advocate, June 1964: a man had been lookout the last two summers
Dismantled in 1979; nothing remains at the site
Registered April 22, 2020; nominated by Brad Eells

notes_for_editor: Built year is disputed: the register gives 1934 and a June 1934 paper says building was about to start, while the Klamath chronology quoted on Forest Lookouts gives 1935 for CCC construction. The story gives both. The record's height of 4.6 m matches the 1952 survey's 'about 15 feet'; the survey describes the house, not the cab floor, so it is treated as overall house height. Status rests on one register line; no later source was found. The 1964 staffing date is the publication date of the paper, not the years worked.
